title: Seoul Central District Court says personal data could be recovered from redacted judgments it posted online
date_note: Dailysecu's article of 23 November gives no date for the court's disclosure; the court notice could not be loaded, so the article's publication day is used.
summary: According to Dailysecu, the Seoul Central District Court said personal data redacted in judgments posted on its "major rulings" page could be recovered by certain editing operations or by having an AI read the file, and that it confirmed exposure in a total of 10 judgments. Dailysecu says the data included resident registration numbers, addresses, criminal records and family relations. The court says it corrected the judgments and posted a notice on its website.
plain: A Seoul court says personal details it had blacked out in rulings posted online, such as ID numbers, could be uncovered in 10 rulings, Dailysecu reports. The court says it fixed the files.
exec: A court says redacted personal data, including resident registration numbers per Dailysecu, could be recovered from 10 judgments it had published online.

sources.name: Dailysecu: 서울중앙지법 판결문 개인정보 유출…다른 법원은 안전한가

evidence.quote: 총 10건에서 개인정보 노출 문제를 확인했다고 밝혔다

validation.note: Only Dailysecu read; it relays the court's own statement. The court's website (seoul.scourt.go.kr) reset the connection on every try, so its notice was not read. Dailysecu says the court did not disclose which file format, editing method or AI tool caused the problem.
